title: Ristna Lighthouse
visualBrief: Bright red concrete-jacketed stair tube with eight full-height ribs, flared foot and upper supports, three horizontal braces, expanded riveted service room with sixteen small ports, scalloped gallery brackets, close picket rail, diamond-glazed lantern and white dome/vane.

sourceFacts.appearance: Maintained red/white exterior; published authority text confirms restoration completion in summer 2026. Small details follow the genuine April 2026 Ristna close photograph and earlier records.
sourceFacts.basis: National aid 673 gives 27.2 m base-relative height and WGS84 location. Society archival 1925 elevation and sections identify eight concrete-jacketed ribs and three braces; cited industrial-heritage record gives a 5 m service drum. Genuine April 2026 Ristna photograph controls fittings, prior to repainting. July 2026 reopening article confirms works in text; its lead photograph depicts Mehikoorma and is excluded as a Ristna visual reference.

geographicProposal.notes: Mapped road is station context; no mapped tower footprint or surveyed doorway azimuth is available. Aerial coastal/station arrangement supports the southeast door quadrant, not a precise bearing. National authority anchor is retained instead of the offset OSM point. Y=0 is host terrain contact; no surveyed foundation elevation, detached station buildings or shoreline is included. Public API returned 429 on 2026-10-09; this review uses the dated 2026-09-28 map snapshot. +Y up; +Z southeast and +X northeast. Entrance quadrant is reconstructed from the inspected 2014 aerial and archival site layout; the eight ribs retain 45-degree rotational symmetry.

limitations: The modeled exterior follows the cited published facts and inspected photographs. Unpublished dimensions and local fittings are explicitly photo-proportioned; no claim of engineering survey accuracy is made.
Portable PBR and shared metric surfaces are provided. Surface weathering, material color under local lighting and fine facade relief require close render review before maximum-detail acceptance.

Detailed exterior follows the documented post1920 concrete jacket, not the original1874 open iron frame. Published total height and5m service drum constrain a photographed/archival component reconstruction. Exact entrance azimuth and minor restored2026 vent fittings are not surveyed. Detached station buildings remain map structures.
referenceRights: Original geometry and shared procedural materials. Official photographs are research references only; no reference imagery or third-party mesh is embedded or redistributed.

nativeAxes.origin: Authored main tower center at local base level; attached ensembles are offset from this origin.

appearance.identity: Red concrete-jacketed eight-rib tower with three braces, expanded 16-port service drum, scalloped gallery, diamond glazing and white dome/vane.
appearance.epoch: Maintained red/white exterior, reconstructed from the operator photograph, genuine April 2026 pre-restoration close photograph, society aerial and archival section.
appearance.master: Preserve the original 68696-triangle master, true holes, radial plates, rail hoops and optical representation.
appearance.browser: Component-resampled street and closeup retain actual holes and stable regular dome facets. Far derivatives retain eight ribs, three braces, sixteen port positions, service drum and white dome; omit rivets, reduce gallery brackets and use opaque glazing.
appearance.exclusions: Surveyed minor fitting dimensions, post-restoration vent changes not shown in the accepted photo, interiors, detached station buildings, operational navigation light and surveyed site terrain.

sourceGeometry.reason: Exact default master retained; model-specific browser subdivision recipe isolated from unrelated ready Baltic assets.

sourceLicense: Original geometry under the repository license. Cited sources retain their own rights; OSM-derived axes/footprint evidence © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0.
materialMethod: Shared canonical material graphs with metric UV repeats in extras.molenSurface; portable glTF PBR factors and vertex colors remain. Dark recesses/lantern panels retain local fallback materials.
